title: Assessment and improvement of the care of severely affected post-infectious ME/CFS patients
summary:
The effects of a Long or Post-COVID illness are enormous for those affected and also for their relatives. It is still not precisely known how many people are affected. Estimates suggest that 5–15% of all individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 are affected, a proportion of whom develop the full clinical picture of ME/CFS (Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome). Their care situation remains partly highly problematic despite the existence of initial treatment guidelines. Outpatient healthcare providers, in particular, often report feeling overwhelmed when providing care. 
Through comprehensive data collection, the Innovation Fund project “Improving the care of people affected by post-COVID syndrome  (LCovB)” aims to determine the prevalence of physician-diagnosed Post-COVID illness and the care situation of individuals affected by Long/Post-COVID, to identify care gaps and barriers, and to derive key points for optimizing healthcare provision particularly in outpatient care for individuals who are severely and chronically ill. The project is supported by an expert panel consisting of professionals and people with lived experience. 
The overall project is divided into four study modules. 
Study module 4 focuses specifically on the care situation of homebound ME/CFS patients, who represent a distinct subgroup of individuals with Post-COVID syndrome (PCS). ME/CFS is an illness that is typically triggered by infectious diseases, including COVID-19. Currently, no treatment options are available, and the severity of the illness can vary. In this module, 15 severely affected individuals will be visited at home for ME/CFS diagnostics. The physical examination and medical history will be conducted, as far as possible, analogously to an outpatient clinic appointment. Ongoing care will be provided by the patient’s general practitioner. In addition, the course of the illness will be documented monthly over a period of six months using standardized questionnaires. 

The results of the individual study modules will be consolidated. Based on this synthesis, practice-oriented recommendations for healthcare provision will be developed in collaboration with the expert panel.

interventions.name: 15 Post-COVID affected patients will be visited at home for ME/CFS diagnostics. The physical examination and medical history will, as far as possible, follow the procedures of an outpatient clinic appointment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Bell score of ≤ 20, meets the Canadian criteria for ME/CFS, resides in the Berlin region, general practitioner is willing to provide shared care, and due to the severity of illness, an in-person visit to our outpatient clinic is not possible.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent; severe comorbid or competing physical or mental illnesses
